All 2026 Formula 1 Drivers Can Now Be Had as LEGO Minifigures for the First Time, Race Cars in Tow
15 photos
Photo: LEGO
It's been two years since the organizers of one of the most intense racing series on the planet, Formula 1, and Danish toy maker LEGO tied the knot, and the gift keeps on giving. Taking advantage of the Las Vegas Grand Prix scheduled for this coming weekend, the partners announced the arrival of something that has never been offered in LEGO form on this scale before.
That would be LEGO minifigure versions of all 22 drivers that have lined up on the starting grid this season, complete with detailed printed helmets and race suits and even their respective names and driver numbers.
Accompanying these plastic drivers are the remade versions of all the 11 cars that have competed this season. They have been updated to mimic this season's regulations and liveries, and they are, just like before, part of the Speed Champions series.
LEGO says the new sets replicating the 2026 F1 season cars and drivers will become available on March 1, 2027, which kind of makes them a little late to the party – as a reminder, the competition's next season kicks off on the weekend of March 12.
Photo: LEGO Even so, here they all are, complete with details about the number of parts and LEGO's internal code. As a side note, all cars are priced on the American market at $29.99, and they can already be pre-ordered by those interested. All cars are sized at 1.5 inches (4 cm) high, 2.5 inches (6 cm) wide, and 7.5 inches (19 cm) long once fully assembled.
LEGO Speed Champions McLaren Mastercard MCL40 F1 Race Car (77269) - 196 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS W17 F1 Race Car (77270) - 216 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 F1 Race Car (77268) - 203 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Scuderia Ferrari HP SF-26 F1 Race Car (77267) - 230 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Atlassian Williams FW48 F1 Race Car (77272) - 231 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Visa Cash App RB VCARB 03 F1 Race Car (77273) - 206 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Aston Martin Aramco AMR26 F1 Race Car (77271) - 199 pieces LEGO Speed Champions TGR Haas VF-26 F1 Race Car (77275) - 209 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Audi Revolut R26 F1 Race Car (77276) - 215 pieces LEGO Speed Champions BWT Alpine A526 F1 Race Car (77274) - 212 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Cadillac MAC-26 F1 Race Car (77277) - 212 pieces When revealing these new sets, LEGO said they are only the beginning of what's to come over the next few months from the partnership with Formula 1 . We'll keep an eye on that and report back once we learn more about it.
Separately, the coming Las Vegas F1 race will be packed with other LEGO things. The minicars the toy maker debuted at the British Grand Prix back in July will be on location, and they carry an undisclosed number of special modifications.
They will be part of the F1 weekend as they'll race with a playful twist, as the toy maker says, referring to who is going to drive them. The identity of the drivers will be made public on LEGO's social media channels in the coming hours.
Photo: LEGO The LEGO Race, as it's called, takes place on Saturday, November 21, when it will hit the Strip with 11 replicas of each of this season's real-world racers, which will complete a lap of the circuit for fun.
LEGO will also be present on the Las Vegas Monorail, where it will deploy a wrapped train along with a station domination at the Flamingo/Caesars Palace station.
It may very well happen that LEGO's presence in Las Vegas will be a tad more exciting than the race itself. I mean, who wouldn't want to see F1 cars race on the Las Vegas streets, but there's really no stake as play, if you really think about it.
Both the season's titles, Drivers' Championship and Constructors' Championship, have already been decided, and with three legs to go, mind you. This season's best driver is Mercedes' Andrea Kimi Antonelli , and the same German carmaker beat Ferrari and Red Bull Racing to the teams’ win.
There are, of course, a lot of points left in the competition, and that may impact the final standings below first place, but the fight for the win is over.
Photo: LEGO Following the Las Vegas race, Formula 1 is heading to Qatar on the last weekend of this month, and the weekend after that to Abu Dhabi for the final leg of this year's competition.
The 2027 season will bring with it a number of changes, including an increase in engine power from 400 kW to 420 kW, a five percent fuel flow increase, and a decrease in the power of the motor-generator unit-kinetic from 350 kW to 300 kW.
The modifications, says F1 , are meant to address issues related to energy management and make qualifying more flat-out. We hope they’ll make races even more interesting.
